confirmed.requirement: Free screening MUST ask whether the matter is open
confirmed.evidence: Two facts carry this. (a) `resolved_timing_bucket` offers a `still_open` option (public-profile-projection.ts:123, 159-162) and the evaluator returns `not_yet` / `case_still_open` for it (evaluator.ts:1399-1404) — present in 51/51. (b) The dedicated `pending_cases` question ("Do you have any open cases right now?") is selected in the free stage in only 25/51 jurisdictions. It is absent from the free stage in AK, AZ, CO, CT, DC, DE, FL, HI, IA, ID, IL, KS, KY, MA, MS, ND, NH, OK, PA, RI, SD, TN, UT, VA, WI, WV (26 jurisdictions) because those profiles place it in a postpay stage, so screening-question-selection.ts:63-64 drops it. Meanwhile `pending_cases` is listed in `UNIVERSAL_PREPAY_FACT_IDS` (src/lib/rcap-engine/route-fact-relevance.ts:29-45) as a fact "every route in the engine reads before it will open a packet", and evaluator.ts:1776 reads `isAffirmative(answers.pending_cases)` as a hard `not_yet` blocker. Because the question is never asked, the value is `undefined`, `isAffirmative` returns false, and the blocker silently passes.
confirmed.gapDetail: `pending_cases` is asked at free screening in only 25/51 jurisdictions; in the other 26 the engine's own universal open-case blocker (evaluator.ts:1776) can never fire, because the fact it reads is never collected. `resolved_timing_bucket`'s `still_open` option is the only remaining coverage, and that question is itself optional (`required: false`) in 20 jurisdictions (CA, CO, CT, DE, HI, IA, IN, KS, KY, MA, MD, MI, ND, NH, NJ, OH, PA, RI, UT, WA).
confirmed.participantImpact: In 26 jurisdictions a participant with an open case can complete free screening without ever being asked, and in 20 jurisdictions can skip the only remaining open-case signal entirely.
confirmed.verifierNote: Reproduced by running the real selector over all 51 compiled profiles. `pending_cases` is selected into the free stage in exactly 25/51, and my absent list matches the auditor's character for character: AK,AZ,CO,CT,DC,DE,FL,HI,IA,ID,IL,KS,KY,MA,MS,ND,NH,OK,PA,RI,SD,TN,UT,VA,WI,WV. In PA the projection classifies pending_cases stage=packet_information lifecyclePhase=postpay_packet_field required=false, so screening-question-selection.ts:63-64 drops it and evaluator.ts:1776's `isAffirmative(answers.pending_cases)` blocker can never fire. `resolved_timing_bucket` is present 51/51 and its `still_open` option does return not_yet/case_still_open (evaluator.ts:1399-1404), but I confirmed it is `required:false` in exactly the 20 named jurisdictions (CA,CO,CT,DE,HI,IA,IN,KS,KY,MA,MD,MI,ND,NH,NJ,OH,PA,RI,UT,WA). No hidden work: the newest blob of screening-question-selection.ts (only 2 versions ever), public-profile-projection.ts, evaluator.ts and every compiled profile is IN-HEAD; `lifecyclePhase` is authored in 0 compiled profiles across all 617 refs. No verifier asserts pending_cases reaches free screening.

confirmed.requirement: Free screening MUST ask whether court-ordered requirements were completed
confirmed.evidence: The broad question is built at src/lib/rcap-engine/public-profile-projection.ts:208-228 ("Have you completed everything the court ordered in this case?") and injected by `withBroadCourtRequirementsGate` (:452-461). It is selected in the free stage in 36/51 jurisdictions; scripts/verify-expungement-court-requirements-gate.mjs passes while itself printing "Profiles with court_requirements_completed: 36". The 15 missing are CA, CO, CT, DE, IA, IN, KY, MA, MD, MI, ND, NH, OH, UT, WA. Root cause is pipeline ordering: `withBroadCourtRequirementsGate` runs at :956-959 and :967-970 but keys off an existing `resolved_timing_bucket` (:454), while `withBroadTimingBucketGate` that creates the bucket runs afterwards at :971 — the comment at :960-966 documents this ordering as deliberate. Of the 15, ten still ask a semantically equivalent fact (`sentence_completion_date` and/or `financial_obligations`): CA, CT, DE, IA, KY, MA, MD, NH, OH, WA. Five ask NO completion fact at all in the free stage: CO, IN, MI, ND, UT (verified by running the selector; e.g. ND's entire free set is ownership_scope, jurisdiction_scope, case_outcome, offense_level, possible_pathway_context, resolved_timing_bucket).
confirmed.gapDetail: CO, IN, MI, ND and UT collect no court-requirements-completed fact at free screening. evaluator.ts:1776 reads `answerText(answers[COURT_REQUIREMENTS_FIELD_ID])` and only blocks on the literal values "no"/"not_sure", so an absent answer passes the completion gate silently. Where `court_requirements_completed` is asked it is `required: false` in 19 jurisdictions (FL, HI, IL, KS, LA, MO, MS, MT, NC, NE, NJ, NV, OK, OR, PA, RI, SD, TX, WV), so it is skippable there too.
confirmed.participantImpact: In five states the participant is never asked whether they finished probation, fines or classes before the engine decides the route; the engine treats silence as "finished".
confirmed.verifierNote: Confirmed by runtime sweep: court_requirements_completed selected in 36/51, absent in exactly CA,CO,CT,DE,IA,IN,KY,MA,MD,MI,ND,NH,OH,UT,WA, and required:false in exactly FL,HI,IL,KS,LA,MO,MS,MT,NC,NE,NJ,NV,OK,OR,PA,RI,SD,TX,WV (19). I independently reproduced the five states that collect NO completion fact at all — CO, IN, MI, ND, UT — by printing their entire free set (ND: ownership_scope, jurisdiction_scope, case_outcome, offense_level, possible_pathway_context, resolved_timing_bucket). The root cause is real and self-documented: withBroadCourtRequirementsGate at :452 returns early unless a `resolved_timing_bucket` question with lifecyclePhase prepay_timing_gate already exists, and the comment at :960-966 explicitly states the bucket is added last on purpose. evaluator.ts:1776 only blocks on literal 'no'/'not_sure', so absence passes. Branch search: newest public-profile-projection.ts blob (3716eba4, 2026-08-27) is IN-HEAD; no ref carries a variant that reorders these gates.

confirmed.requirement: Facts belong to exactly one stage — the free stage must not depend on facts it does not collect
confirmed.evidence: Two enforcement layers disagree about the same questions. `questionLifecycle.completionAliasIds` (present in 51/51 compiled profiles; `sentence_completion_date` in 25, `financial_obligations` in 22) causes those questions to be DROPPED from the rendered free set at src/lib/rcap-engine/screening-question-selection.ts:61-62. But `projectPublicProfile` still classifies them `prepay_hard_disqualifier` / `prepay_required` with `required: true`, and `requiredMissingPublicQuestionIds` (src/lib/rcap-engine/answer-normalization.ts:50-58, filtered by `isPrepaymentQuestion` at :83-86) still demands them — called from evaluator.ts:392-397, which returns `needs_more_info` / `missing_required_facts`. I reproduced this end to end: for Alabama, answering all eleven questions the selector actually renders (ownership_scope, jurisdiction_scope, case_outcome, offense_level, possible_pathway_context, trafficking_status, pardon_status, pending_cases, resolved_timing_bucket, court_requirements_completed='yes', state_exclusion_categories='None of these') returns `resultCode: needs_more_info, paymentAllowed: false, missingQuestionIds: ['sentence_completion_date','financial_obligations']` — both `renderedInFree=false`. Sweeping all 51 jurisdictions with the same method, 29 hit this: AK, AL, AR, AZ, DC, FL, GA, ID, IL, KS, LA, ME, MO, MT, NC, NE, NJ, NM, NY, OK, OR, SC, SD, TN, TX, VT, WI, WV, WY. The result screen then lists the unanswerable question (ScreeningResult.tsx:152, 216-226) and offers a fix button wired to `onEditAnswers(missing[0])` (ScreeningResult.tsx:291-295) → `goToQuestions` in ScreeningFlow.tsx:398-408, whose `screens.findIndex(...)` returns -1 for a question that was never a screen, so no navigation occurs and pressing Continue re-evaluates to the identical result.
confirmed.gapDetail: There is no alias resolution: nothing maps `court_requirements_completed` back onto the `completionAliasIds` it replaced, and nothing clears `required` on an aliased question in the projection. I searched history and all 617 remote branches (`git log --all -S'completionAlias' -- src/lib/rcap-engine/answer-normalization.ts src/lib/rcap-engine/evaluator.ts` returns nothing; the only non-HEAD variants of answer-normalization.ts are from June 2026 and are all merged ancestors). The fix does not exist anywhere in the repository.
confirmed.participantImpact: In 29 of 51 jurisdictions a participant who answers every free-screening question correctly gets "we need more information", is shown a fact they were never asked for, and clicking the fix button does nothing — the free product is an unrecoverable loop.
confirmed.verifierNote: I reproduced this end to end and got the identical 29-jurisdiction list: AK,AL,AR,AZ,DC,FL,GA,ID,IL,KS,LA,ME,MO,MT,NC,NE,NJ,NM,NY,OK,OR,SC,SD,TN,TX,VT,WI,WV,WY. Answering every question the selector renders (including the route-reveal second pass) returns resultCode=needs_more_info, paymentAllowed=false, missingQuestionIds containing sentence_completion_date and/or financial_obligations — questions the selector dropped via completionAliasIds. The runtime path is confirmed: /api/expungement-ai/screening/progress calls selectScreeningQuestionIds, /api/expungement-ai/evaluate calls evaluateAuthoritativeScreeningResult -> evaluateAgainstProfile -> requiredMissingPublicQuestionIds. I also confirmed the dead fix button: goToQuestions (ScreeningFlow.tsx:398-408) does `screens.findIndex(...)`, which is -1 for a question that was never a screen, so setCurrentIndex is never called and only setPhase('questions') runs. Exhaustive branch search confirms no fix exists: screening-question-selection.ts has only 2 blobs in all history (newest IN-HEAD), answer-normalization.ts only 4 (newest 2026-07-01, IN-HEAD), evaluator.ts newest IN-HEAD; `git log --all -S` for aliasSatisfied/resolveCompletionAlias/completionAliasSatisfied/satisfiesAlias returns 0 commits each. The defect was introduced by 3716eba4 'fix(rcap): keep exact route dates postpay' (2026-08-27), which is IN-HEAD.

confirmed.requirement: Choosing a specific remedy must PRUNE questions belonging only to rejected remedies
confirmed.evidence: The mechanism is `questionLifecycle.routeConsumers` gating at src/lib/rcap-engine/screening-question-selection.ts:66-70: a question with a non-empty consumer list is shown only when the selected pathway is one of its consumers. This is reveal-gating, not pruning — I measured that in all 51 profiles no route context ever selects FEWER questions than the no-route baseline (e.g. CA baseline 11, per-route 11/14/15; NY 9 baseline, 9/10/16; DC 8/9; HI 8/9; IN 7/8; WI 10/12). `routeConsumers` is populated in only 8 of 51 profiles — CA (4 entries), DC (2), HI (1), IN (1), MD (2), MO (1), NY (8), WI (2) — and is an empty object `{}` in the other 43, so in those 43 jurisdictions no question is route-conditional at all. The verifier scripts/verify-rcap-prepay-question-gate.mjs:141-144 only asserts the reveal direction (a route-consumer question must not leak outside its consumers); it asserts nothing about pruning.
confirmed.gapDetail: Pruning-on-remedy-choice is not implemented as such; the equivalent outcome is achieved only for the 15 route-scoped questions across 8 states by hiding them until their route is chosen. For the 43 profiles with empty `routeConsumers`, selecting a remedy changes nothing about which questions are asked. This is only harmless because the surviving free question set is already reduced to shared discriminators (see previous finding); it is not enforced by any mechanism.
confirmed.participantImpact: Choosing a remedy never shortens the questionnaire; it can only lengthen it. No state prunes.
confirmed.verifierNote: Measured directly: across all 51 profiles, for every pathway label, the selected question count is NEVER lower than the no-route baseline — 0/51 profiles ever prune. Six expand: CA 11->15, NY 9->16, WI 10->12, DC 8->9, HI 8->9, IN 7->8. I confirmed routeConsumers is non-empty in exactly 8 profiles (CA 4, DC 2, HI 1, IN 1, MD 2, MO 1, NY 8, WI 2 — 21 entries, slightly more than the auditor's 15) and is `{}` in the other 43, so remedy choice changes nothing there. The verifier only asserts the reveal direction (a route-consumer question must not leak outside its consumers) and says nothing about pruning. No branch carries a pruning implementation: screening-question-selection.ts has 2 blobs total and HEAD holds the newer.

confirmed.requirement: A stale-rejected-route fact suppression mechanism exists
confirmed.evidence: Two real mechanisms exist. (1) Evaluation-side: `ambiguityReason` (src/lib/rcap-engine/evaluator.ts:664-682) filters candidate blocking facts through `relevantFactIds(profile, selectedPathway)` (route-fact-relevance.ts:145-152), so an "I'm not sure" left over from a rejected route no longer escalates. I verified this: in California, evaluating the Tool-1 dismissal/set-aside route with `ca_prop64_branch: 'I am not sure'` and `ca_prop64_qualifying_marijuana_offense: 'I am not sure'` still returns `packet_ready_with_caution, paymentAllowed=true` — identical to the clean run — because `pathwayRelevantFactIds` reports `ca_prop64_branch` as relevant only to the two Prop 64 pathways. The module's header comment (route-fact-relevance.ts:8-21) documents this exact defect being fixed. (2) Display-side: `sanitizeAnswersForQuestionIds` (src/components/expungement-ai/screening/screens.ts:66-79) drops an answer once its question was previously rendered and is no longer selected, and `sanitizeResumedAnswersForQuestionIds` (:82-96) treats every prepay question as prior UI state so a resumed branch answer is dropped.
confirmed.gapDetail: Both mechanisms are partial. The suppression only neutralises AMBIGUITY (`isExplicitUnknownAnswer`); a stale definite value is still passed to the engine and is only safe because route-specific gates are keyed by `<JURISDICTION>:<pathwayId>` (`ROUTE_ESCALATION_FACT_IDS`, route-fact-relevance.ts:50-76 and `routeSpecificSafetyGate`). More importantly the answer-deletion is CLIENT-ONLY: every server write path accepts and persists whatever answers are posted. src/app/api/expungement-ai/evaluate/route.ts:28-33 forwards `body.answers` verbatim, and `validatePublicAnswerQuestionIds` (answer-normalization.ts:65-68) only rejects ids unknown to the public profile — it accepts answers to postpay-stage questions (`disposition_date`, `court`, `case_identifier`) submitted during free screening. src/app/api/expungement-ai/screening/pending/route.ts:22-27,74 stores `body.answers` unfiltered into `consumer_pending_screening_results.screening_answers`, and src/app/api/expungement-ai/screening/save-resume/route.ts:22-33,58-72 persists `payload.answers` with no question-id or stage validation at all.
confirmed.participantImpact: A stale not-sure from an abandoned route no longer blocks the participant. But nothing on the server prevents free-stage exact-fact answers from being written and stored, so the separation is a rendering property, not a data property.
confirmed.verifierNote: Both mechanisms the auditor credits do exist and I verified their code. ambiguityReason (evaluator.ts:664-682) filters candidate blocking facts through relevantFactIds(profile, selectedPathway); route-fact-relevance.ts's header comment documents the exact Prop 64 / Hawaii defect being fixed and scopes packetGenerator collection to the route's own entry. sanitizeAnswersForQuestionIds and sanitizeResumedAnswersForQuestionIds exist as described. The gap is also real and I confirmed it: the deletion is client-only. validatePublicAnswerQuestionIds accepted {disposition_date, court, case_identifier, county_or_filing_location} for AL, TX and NY with zero rejections (CA rejected only county_or_filing_location). screening/pending/route.ts writes `screening_answers: body.answers` verbatim, and save-resume/route.ts checks only `payload.answers` is present before handing the whole object to saveScreeningResumeLink. PARTIAL is correct.

confirmed.requirement: Back navigation recomputes the route
confirmed.evidence: `handleBack` (src/components/expungement-ai/screening/ScreeningFlow.tsx:389-396) only does `setCurrentIndex(index - 1)` (or pushes to the state picker at index 0). It does not call `requestScreeningProgress` and does not recompute `questionIds`. Recomputation happens on the next forward step: `handleContinue` (:356-387) POSTs the full current answer map to /api/expungement-ai/screening/progress (:367), re-projects the screens (:374), sanitizes stale answers (:375) and re-derives the cursor position from the NEW list (:379-382), so an answer changed after going back does drive a fresh route selection. The same recompute runs on mount/resume (:215-236) and on save-progress (:414-421). Server-side, route identity is always re-derived from stored answers and never trusted from the client (src/lib/expungement-ai/screening-session-route-identity.ts:9-19,29-52; src/lib/expungement-ai/authoritative-screening-result.ts:11-17,38-40; src/app/api/expungement-ai/evaluate/route.ts:20-25 rejects any client-asserted route identity).
confirmed.gapDetail: Between pressing Back and pressing Continue the rendered screen list is stale, so a participant who goes back and changes `possible_pathway_context` can still see and answer questions belonging to the remedy they just abandoned until the next Continue. `goToQuestions` (:398-408), the Edit path from the result screen, also re-enters the questionnaire against the stale `screens` array without recomputing.
confirmed.participantImpact: The route is always recomputed before it matters (evaluation, save, payment), but the questionnaire can briefly display abandoned-route questions after a Back.
confirmed.verifierNote: Read the source directly. handleBack does only setError(null) then setCurrentIndex(index-1), or router.push(PICKER_PATH) at index 0 — no requestScreeningProgress, no questionIds recompute. handleContinue does POST progress, screensFromQuestionIds, sanitizeAnswersForQuestionIds, setQuestionIds, then re-derives the cursor from the new list, so the route is recomputed on the next forward step; handleSaveProgress does the same. Server-side route identity is genuinely server-owned: /api/expungement-ai/evaluate rejects client-asserted route identity via forbiddenRouteIdentityFields and forwards only the four client fields. goToQuestions does re-enter against the stale `screens` array. PARTIAL is exactly right — the route is recomputed before it matters, but the rendered list is stale between Back and Continue.

confirmed.requirement: The client-side profile bundle must agree with the server's stage classification (defence in depth)
confirmed.evidence: src/lib/expungement-ai/frontend/profiles/all51.json is statically imported into the screening client bundle (src/lib/expungement-ai/frontend/profile-loader.ts:17, 27) and is stale relative to the engine: it has 728 questions with `lifecyclePhase: undefined` and, critically, assigns `disposition_date` (type `date_or_unknown`) the stage `timing_and_completion` — a PREPAY stage — in 30 jurisdictions (AK, AL, AR, AZ, DC, FL, GA, ID, IL, LA, ME, MN, MO, MT, NC, NE, NM, NV, NY, OK, OR, SC, SD, TN, TX, VA, VT, WI, WV, WY), whereas the engine projection classifies it `postpay_packet_field` / `packet_information`. It also carries `court` (type `text`), `case_identifier`, `county_or_filing_location` and `charge` — 216 exact-fact questions in total. Applying the client's own `deriveScreens`/`isPrepayQuestion` rule (src/components/expungement-ai/screening/screens.ts:19-40) to that bundle renders `disposition_date` as a free screening question in those 30 states.
confirmed.gapDetail: The bundle is not currently rendered because `USE_LIVE_PROFILE_ENDPOINT = true` (profile-loader.ts:25) and `screensFromQuestionIds` intersects with the server list, so the only live consumers are `listAvailableStateKeys`/`listAvailableJurisdictions` (:38-63) and `sanitizeResumedAnswersForQuestionIds`. But the client-side backstop is defeated: if the flow ever fell back to `loadMockProfile` (:82-88) or `deriveScreens`, an exact disposition date would render in the free stage in 30 jurisdictions, and the file's stale comment at profile-loader.ts:93 ("Not active on this branch") contradicts the flag two lines above it.
confirmed.participantImpact: No participant impact today; the second line of defence is silently wrong in 30 states and would leak an exact date if it ever became the primary.
confirmed.verifierNote: Parsed the bundle: 728 questions, and ALL 728 lack lifecyclePhase. disposition_date appears in exactly 30 jurisdictions — AK,AL,AR,AZ,DC,FL,GA,ID,IL,LA,ME,MN,MO,MT,NC,NE,NM,NV,NY,OK,OR,SC,SD,TN,TX,VA,VT,WI,WV,WY — always with stage `timing_and_completion`, which is not in the client's own postpay drop list ['record_readiness','case_details','packet_information'], so deriveScreens would render it in the free stage. I counted 205 exact-fact rows (disposition_date/court/case_identifier/county_or_filing_location/charge/county) versus the auditor's 216 — immaterial to the finding. The engine projection classifies disposition_date as stage=packet_information lifecyclePhase=postpay_packet_field. The stale comment at profile-loader.ts:93 ('Not active on this branch') does contradict USE_LIVE_PROFILE_ENDPOINT = true two lines above. The bundle's newest blob is f847934 (2026-07-01) and is IN-HEAD; no branch carries a refreshed one. No participant impact today, backstop silently wrong — PARTIAL is right.

confirmed.requirement: The affordance by which a participant chooses a specific remedy must be honestly presented
confirmed.evidence: `possible_pathway_context` is the remedy-choice question and is genuinely route-determinative: `selectPathway` matches on it exactly before any heuristic (src/lib/rcap-engine/evaluator.ts:698-706) and `selectScreeningQuestionIds` keys all route-scoped reveal off it (screening-question-selection.ts:47-52, 66-70). The projection's own comment says so: "the evaluator's pathway selection matches on it exactly before falling back to token heuristics… the participant is routed to a different remedy than the one they came for — silently" (public-profile-projection.ts:416-433). Yet the compiled profiles publish it with `contextOnly: true` and `doesNotSelectPathway: true` in all 51 (verified in CA-california.json and LA-louisiana.json question rows; my runtime sweep found it `contextOnly` in 51/51 public profiles), and `required: false`. Because `contextOnly` is true, the UI renders ContextOnlyBanner (src/components/expungement-ai/screening/ContextOnlyBanner.tsx:16-20): "Optional. This question is just for context. It does not decide your result and you can skip it." It is also excluded from `blocksContinue` (src/components/expungement-ai/screening/answers.ts:61-65) and from ambiguity escalation (evaluator.ts:675 filters `contextOnly !== true`).
confirmed.gapDetail: The single question that implements 'choosing a specific remedy' is labelled as not deciding the result. The contract's pruning/scoping rule is predicated on the participant choosing a remedy; the UI actively discourages answering it.
confirmed.participantImpact: A participant is told the remedy-selection question does not decide anything and can be skipped; skipping it leaves them on heuristic routing and on the widest question set.
confirmed.verifierNote: Verified every leg. selectPathway matches possible_pathway_context exactly before statute-number and token heuristics. selectScreeningQuestionIds:47-52 keys all route-scoped reveal off it. The projection's own comment at :416-433 says verbatim that where the option list omits a pathway 'the participant is routed to a different remedy than the one they came for — silently'. Yet my runtime sweep found contextOnly === true on possible_pathway_context in 51/51 public profiles, doesNotSelectPathway:true in all 51 compiled files, and required:false in 51/51. ContextOnlyBanner renders 'Optional. This question is just for context. It does not decide your result and you can skip it.' blocksContinue returns false for any contextOnly question regardless of required, and ambiguityReason filters contextOnly !== true. The one question that implements remedy choice is published as non-deciding. CONTRADICTED confirmed.

confirmed.requirement: Free screening asks pending-case and prior-relief facts when route-determinative
confirmed.evidence: `prior_relief` ("Have you had a record cleared before, anywhere?") reaches free screening in only 14/51 jurisdictions (present in FL, GA, IL-adjacent set measured at runtime; absent in AK, AL, AR, AZ, CA, CO, CT, DC, DE, HI, IL, IN, KS, KY, LA, MA, ME, MN, MS, ND, NE, NH, NM, NV, NY, OH, OK, OR, PA, RI, SD, TX, UT, VA, VT, WA, WI). `pardon_status` reaches it in 25/51. `state_exclusion_categories` — the threshold exclusion screen the evaluator reads at evaluator.ts:648-661 to return `likely_not_eligible` / `state_exclusion_unknown` — reaches free screening in only 21/51 (absent in DC, HI, IA, ID, IN, KS, KY, LA, MA, ME, MN, MS, MT, ND, NE, NH, NM, NV, OH, OK, PA, RI, SC, SD, UT, VT, WA, WI, WV, WY). Two facts the engine treats as universal blockers are asked in ZERO of 51: `new_convictions_during_waiting_period` (read at evaluator.ts:985 and :1776) and `special_preconditions_confirmed` (read at evaluator.ts:1789, where a negative or unknown answer returns `needs_review`) — both are listed in `UNIVERSAL_PREPAY_FACT_IDS` (route-fact-relevance.ts:29-45) but are classified into `packet_information` in every compiled profile and dropped by screening-question-selection.ts:63-64.
confirmed.gapDetail: `new_convictions_during_waiting_period` and `special_preconditions_confirmed` are dead facts at the free stage in all 51 jurisdictions: the code that reads them can never see a value, so `isAffirmative`/`isNegative`/`isExplicitUnknownAnswer` all return false and the gates at evaluator.ts:1776 and :1789 silently pass. `prior_relief` (14/51) and `state_exclusion_categories` (21/51) are route-determinative in far more states than they are asked.
confirmed.participantImpact: A participant who picked up a new conviction during the waiting period, or who has not met a source-listed precondition, sails through the free check; the two gates written to catch that never receive an answer.
confirmed.verifierNote: Runtime sweep confirms every number: prior_relief free-stage in 14/51, pardon_status 25/51, state_exclusion_categories 21/51 with the auditor's exact absent list, and new_convictions_during_waiting_period + special_preconditions_confirmed in 0/51. I confirmed the mechanism: both are defined in the projection (lines 634 and 678) with stage `timing_and_completion` and required:false, but lifecyclePhaseForQuestion's runtime regex classifies them postpay_packet_field (PA: stage=packet_information lifecyclePhase=postpay_packet_field), so screening-question-selection.ts:63-64 drops them platform-wide. The gates at evaluator.ts:1776 (isAffirmative new_convictions) and :1789 (isNegative/isExplicitUnknownAnswer special_preconditions) therefore never receive a value. No verifier asserts they are asked — the only script references (verify-rcap-ratified-route-payment.mjs, verify-rcap-no-generic-fallbacks.mjs, verify-corrections-a-boundaries.mjs) inject synthetic answers directly into evaluateScreening, bypassing the selector, which is precisely why the verifiers stay green while the free stage never collects them.

confirmed.requirement: Distinct FREE_SCREENING / PACKET_INFORMATION / FINAL_VERIFICATION / POST_PAYMENT fact buckets
confirmed.evidence: Stage 1 and stage 2 are real and separated. PACKET_INFORMATION is an auth-gated surface: src/app/api/expungement-ai/briefcase/[itemId]/packet-information/route.ts:24-33 requires an authenticated owner and an owned Briefcase item, and its field set comes from `postPaymentPacketCompletion` (src/lib/expungement-ai/packet-information.ts:1289-1302), which the projection builds by lifecycle phase (public-profile-projection.ts:492-503). But the taxonomy only has two real buckets. The `lifecyclePhase` enum (src/lib/rcap-engine/contracts.ts:91-104) has five `prepay_*` values and seven `postpay_*` values plus `optional_or_later`/`guidance_only`, with NO value distinguishing FINAL_VERIFICATION facts from POST_PAYMENT facts, and `allPublicQuestions` (packet-information.ts:1289-1302) pulls all eight postpay groups — including `serviceOrMailingFields` and `filingReadinessFields` — into the same pre-payment packet-information surface. There is no fact bucket collected after payment: packet-information.ts contains no payment-conditioned field gating (`paymentAllowed` appears only as a readiness/consistency check at :737, :1135, :1153-1157). FINAL_VERIFICATION (src/lib/expungement-ai/verification-cas.ts) consumes facts and writes a snapshot; it collects none.
confirmed.gapDetail: The contract's four fact stages are implemented as two (prepay screening vs postpay packet completion). FINAL_VERIFICATION and POST_PAYMENT exist as processes, not as fact stages, so there is no classification that could mark a fact as 'ask only at final verification' or 'ask only after payment'.
confirmed.participantImpact: Everything not in free screening is asked at once in packet information, before payment; nothing is deferred to verification or to after payment.
confirmed.verifierNote: Confirmed. The lifecyclePhase enum has 14 values — 5 prepay_*, 7 postpay_*, optional_or_later, guidance_only — and none distinguishes a final-verification fact from a post-payment fact. allPublicQuestions (packet-information.ts:1289-1302) pulls all eight postpay groups including serviceOrMailingFields and filingReadinessFields into one surface. The packet-information route is genuinely auth-gated (auth_required 401, then getBriefcaseItem ownership check), so stages 1 and 2 are real. But grepping paymentAllowed in packet-information.ts shows it only at :482, :712, :737, :1020, :1135, :1153-1157 as readiness/consistency checks — never as field gating, so no fact is deferred until after payment. FINAL_VERIFICATION exists only as a status/reason string (packet-information.ts:337,446,780,795; briefcase-presentation-authority.ts:407; pending/claim/route.ts:241) and as a docs-only phrase introduced by commits a6ec079e/84319f19 — never as a fact classification. Two real buckets, not four.

confirmed.requirement: Server-side enforcement that free-stage submissions carry only free-stage facts
confirmed.evidence: No write path validates the stage of a submitted answer. `evaluateScreening` calls `validatePublicAnswerQuestionIds` (src/lib/rcap-engine/evaluator.ts:367-368 → src/lib/rcap-engine/answer-normalization.ts:65-68), which builds its valid set from `publicProfile.questions` plus `flowStages.questionIds` — that includes every postpay question — so a free-screening POST carrying `disposition_date`, `court`, `case_identifier` or `record_documents` is accepted, evaluated and persisted. src/app/api/expungement-ai/evaluate/route.ts:28-33 rejects only client-asserted ROUTE identity (`forbiddenRouteIdentityFields`, :22-25), not out-of-stage facts. src/app/api/expungement-ai/screening/pending/route.ts:74 writes `screening_answers: body.answers` verbatim. src/app/api/expungement-ai/screening/save-resume/route.ts:31-33 checks only that `answers` is present, then hands the whole object to `saveScreeningResumeLink` (:58-72) — no id validation, no stage validation, no size-per-field limit beyond the 40 KB payload cap.
confirmed.gapDetail: Stage separation is enforced only on the READ path (which questions the server tells the client to render). There is no corresponding enforcement on the WRITE path, so the guarantee is a rendering guarantee, not a data guarantee. I searched history and branches: `git log --all -S'validatePublicAnswerQuestionIds'` and the blob survey of answer-normalization.ts across all remote branches show no variant that filters by stage; the only non-HEAD versions are merged June 2026 ancestors.
confirmed.participantImpact: An assisted-intake surface, a modified client, or any future caller can write exact court and case-number facts into the anonymous pre-account screening row, defeating the point of the free/paid fact boundary.
confirmed.verifierNote: Directly falsified the possibility of a hidden implementation. I called validatePublicAnswerQuestionIds with {disposition_date, court, case_identifier, county_or_filing_location}: AL, TX and NY rejected NOTHING; CA rejected only county_or_filing_location (unknown to that profile), still accepting disposition_date, court and case_identifier. The valid set is built from publicProfile.questions plus flowStages.questionIds (answer-normalization.ts:74-80), which includes every postpay question. /api/expungement-ai/evaluate rejects only client-asserted route identity, not out-of-stage facts. /api/expungement-ai/screening/pending writes `screening_answers: body.answers` verbatim after only isScreeningAnswers shape validation. /api/expungement-ai/screening/save-resume validates only that jurisdiction, answers and a string email are present, then persists the whole object; the only bound is the 40 KB payload cap. Grepping scripts/ and src/ for validatePublicAnswerQuestionIds / out_of_stage / outOfStage / stage_violation returns only the two engine files and two unrelated launch verifiers. `git log --all -S` for stageForWrite/validateAnswerStage/assertFreeStageAnswers returns 0 commits. answer-normalization.ts has 4 blobs in all history and HEAD holds the newest. MISSING is correct.

confirmed.requirement: The legacy RCAP partner intake must observe the same free-stage boundary
confirmed.evidence: The legacy partner path (`/intake/[partnerSlug]` → `/documents/[partnerSlug]/form`) does not use the rcap-engine selector at all; its free-stage questions are a hardcoded list in src/lib/rcap-intake/questions.ts:11-72. Most of it is contract-compliant: `approximate_case_year` ("About when did this happen? You can enter a year or an approximate timeframe", :50-55), `has_documents` (":57-62, "Do not upload documents here. We are only asking whether you have them"), broad `case_outcome` (:36-49). But :32-36 asks `county` — "What county or local area was involved?" — at the free stage, whereas the national engine classifies `county` / `county_or_filing_location` as an exact packet fact confined to `packet_information` (`exactPacketFactIds` contains `county` in 13 profiles and `county_or_filing_location` in 32). The exact court/case-number collection is correctly deferred to the post-intake form surface (src/app/documents/[partnerSlug]/form/MississippiPetitionInformationForm.tsx:123-132, TexasHarrisPetitionInformationForm.tsx:111-117, DcMotionInformationForm.tsx:115, IllinoisPetitionInformationForm.tsx:100), which is gated on an existing intake session (src/app/documents/[partnerSlug]/form/page.tsx:72-78).
confirmed.gapDetail: Two screening surfaces disagree on whether county/filing location is a free-stage or packet-stage fact. The legacy intake has no lifecycle metadata, no stage classifier and no verifier coverage in this dimension.
confirmed.participantImpact: A partner-program participant on the legacy path is asked for the county at the free stage, which the national engine treats as a post-screening packet fact.

confirmed.requirement: Outcome 1 — 'possible packet path' is represented in the engine and the UI.
confirmed.evidence: Engine: src/lib/rcap-engine/contracts.ts:1-10 declares packet_ready and packet_ready_with_caution; evaluator.ts:598-600 selects between them. UI: ScreeningResult.tsx:30-32 and :91. But the two are effectively indistinguishable above the fold — ScreeningResult.tsx:31 eyebrow "A path may be available" vs :32 "A path may be available." differ only by a full stop, both use the same CheckCircle2 icon, and :167 gives both the identical h1 "You may be able to prepare an expungement packet." Only the tone colour (:80-86) and the presence of a cautions block (:198-214) differ. Separately, the CTA is inverted against the contract: the contract text says a packet-path result offers "Save this matter and continue", but ScreeningResult.tsx:69-70 gives packet-ready "Save to my Briefcase and continue" while :71-77 gives that exact string to needs_more_info, not_yet, needs_review, likely_not_eligible and hard_stop.
confirmed.gapDetail: packet_ready and packet_ready_with_caution are not visually separable, and the contract's packet-path CTA string is attached to the non-packet outcomes instead. Both are fixed on origin/claude/expai-flow-corrections-p4 (see the UNMERGED finding below).
confirmed.participantImpact: A participant whose route carries statutory cautions sees the same headline, icon and subheading as one with a clean route; nothing above the cautions list signals that the route is qualified.
confirmed.verifierNote: Confirmed, and the auditor UNDERSTATED it. The eyebrow strings at :31/:32 are never what renders — translate() resolves the keys at :43-44, and src/lib/expungement-ai/localization.ts:91-92 defines BOTH 'result.path_available' and 'result.path_available_caution' as the byte-identical string 'A path may be available.' in en AND 'Puede haber una ruta disponible.' in es. So the two packet-ready codes are not distinguishable even by the trailing full stop the auditor found; they are literally identical, in both locales, plus identical CheckCircle2 icon and identical h1 (result.packet_title, localization.ts:86, which is also the same sentence). Only TONE_ACCENT (:80-86) and the cautions block differ. CTA inversion also confirmed: docs/product-flows/expungement-ai-dtc-user-flow.md:48 says 'A packet-ready result uses the primary action Save this matter and continue', while ScreeningResult.tsx:69-70 gives packet-ready 'Save to my Briefcase and continue' and :71-77 hands 'Save this matter and continue' to needs_more_info/needs_review/not_yet/likely_not_eligible/hard_stop. CORRECTION the auditor missed: the doc it relies on is no longer the authority. Commit a6ec079e ('docs: make the Grade-A product contract the authority') installed docs/PRODUCT_CONTRACT.md and deleted the condensed contract; PRODUCT_CONTRACT.md:311-317 specifies the primary action as 'Save my result and continue' — a third string that neither HEAD nor the unmerged p4 branch implements. The gap is real and slightly worse than reported.

confirmed.requirement: Outcome 4 — 'automatic or no-filing' is a distinct preliminary outcome.
confirmed.evidence: The engine detects the condition explicitly and structurally — src/lib/rcap-engine/evaluator.ts:462-468 and :532-537 call routeIsAutomaticOrNoFiling and emit reason code `<jur>.automatic_or_no_filing_route` with guidanceTextForPathway — but it collapses onto resultCode "guidance_only", so there is no distinct code in contracts.ts:1-10 and no distinct branch in ScreeningResult.tsx:30-40 / :42-52 / :68-78. The only participant-visible differentiator is indirect: those branches attach the pathway's packetPlan (:466, :535), and ScreeningResult.tsx:244 → PacketPlanSummary → packetBodyText at :320-324 renders "We'll help you confirm automatic relief and what to do next." for mode automatic_relief_verification_and_guidance. Both automatic and ordinary guidance share eyebrow "Next steps for your state" (:35), the same Info icon, the same "Save this guidance" CTA (:73) and the same careState guidance_only (frontend/briefcase-presentation.ts:68-70, :113-118).
confirmed.gapDetail: There is no `automatic_or_no_filing` result code and no dedicated result-card treatment. The distinction survives only in the reason text and in a packet-plan-mode sentence, and is lost entirely once the matter is saved — briefcase-presentation.ts:113-118 shows the same "Next steps saved" badge and blurb for both.
confirmed.participantImpact: A participant on a route where relief happens automatically with nothing to file reads the same card, badge and CTA as one on a route where we simply cannot sell them a packet — they are not told plainly that no filing is required of them.
confirmed.verifierNote: Confirmed. No 'automatic_or_no_filing' member exists in ScreeningResultCode (contracts.ts:1-10) and no branch in ScreeningResult.tsx. Both call sites collapse to guidance_only. I searched all 617 branches for a distinct code and found none. I DID find two things the auditor missed, and neither rescues the outcome: (1) scripts/verify-legal-authority-contracts.mjs:131-137 does enforce the outcome at the legal-authority layer — 'automatic or no-filing relief must not open checkout' — and it PASSES (exit 0, 50 decisions / 127 route contracts), so the payment consequence of the outcome is real and verified; (2) data/expungement-ai/corrections-a/runtime-fixtures.json carries an explicit closureCategory of 'automatic_or_no_filing' on four routes, checked by scripts/verify-corrections-a-closure.mjs:115-116,227. But `grep -rn closureCategory src/` returns ZERO hits — that taxonomy has no runtime consumer and never reaches a participant. The only participant-visible trace remains evaluator.ts:1444's generic reason text ('The selected source-defined route is automatic or guidance-only', softened to 'state route' by missing-fields.ts) plus the packetPlan-mode sentence. The auditor's finding stands.

confirmed.requirement: Outcome 6 — 'attorney review or referral' is represented in the engine and the UI.
confirmed.evidence: The engine has the outcome: src/lib/rcap-engine/evaluator.ts:575-576 returns needs_review with reason `legal_authority_referral_required` ("This route is limited to attorney-review referral...") when legalContract.outcomeMode === "referral", and :622-623 emits `legal_authority_attorney_review_required` for paymentAuthority "attorney_review_required" (declared in contracts.ts:202). The participant-facing presentation contradicts it. evaluator.ts:1534 sets needs_review's userLabel to "We need one more detail before we can prepare the right packet." — byte-identical to needs_more_info's label at :1532 — and :1549 gives next steps ["Gather court records.", "Save the result.", "Save your progress and update your answers when you have that detail."] with no mention of an attorney or legal aid. Commit 8b6213ac ("fix(expungement): improve Mississippi result path and consumer copy", in HEAD) is what changed it: it replaced "The answers require source review before a packet decision." with the needs-info label and replaced the next step "Get source review before any filing packet is generated." with "Save your progress and update your answers when you have that detail." The client compounds it: src/lib/expungement-ai/missing-fields.ts:104-110 (a client-reachable module — no server-only import, imported by the "use client" ScreeningResult.tsx:21) rewrites ANY engine text matching /source review|packet decision|compiled source rule|deterministic compiled|evaluator|diagnostic/i into "We need one more detail before we can prepare the right packet.", and :122-124 rewrites the old attorney-referral next step into "Save your progress and update your answers when you have that detail." This swallows evaluator.ts:594 ("The matched compiled source rule requires review before a packet decision.") and :1825 ("The source-specific waiting period needs review before a packet decision."). ScreeningResult.tsx:38 shows eyebrow "This needs review" but with the info tone and HelpCircle, and :60/:72 route it into the same "more info" lane as needs_more_info. Briefcase: frontend/briefcase-presentation.ts:78-79 folds needs_review into careState needs_attention and :94 into "We need a little more information". Only the dead ResultPanel.tsx:82-90 still says "consider legal aid or attorney review".
confirmed.gapDetail: The referral/attorney-review outcome exists in the engine but has no distinct participant-facing presentation anywhere on the live screening or Briefcase path. Its label, next steps and reason text are all rewritten into needs-more-information language, first in the engine (8b6213ac) and again in the browser (missing-fields.ts:104-124).
confirmed.participantImpact: A participant on a route the engine has decided is limited to attorney referral, or whose waiting rule could not be executed at all, is told "We need one more detail before we can prepare the right packet" and "Save your progress and update your answers when you have that detail" — invited to keep editing answers to unlock a packet that no answer can unlock, and never told that a lawyer or legal aid is the actual next step. Per the unmerged flow-audit baseline this is the largest single non-guidance terminal in the product (160 of 622 enumerated flows).
confirmed.verifierNote: Confirmed byte-for-byte. evaluator.ts labelForResult gives needs_more_info and needs_review the IDENTICAL string 'We need one more detail before we can prepare the right packet.' nextStepsForResult gives needs_review ['Gather court records.', 'Save the result.', 'Save your progress and update your answers when you have that detail.'] — no attorney, no legal aid — while hard_stop, not_covered_yet and likely_not_eligible all DO carry a legal-aid step, proving the omission is specific to needs_review and not a house style. missing-fields.ts:104-110 confirms the second rewrite in the browser (broad regex /source review|packet decision|compiled source rule|deterministic compiled|evaluator|diagnostic/i), reachable from the 'use client' ScreeningResult. I searched history and branches for a needs_review referral presentation and found none merged. ONE CORRECTION: the auditor calls ResultPanel.tsx 'dead'. It is not dead — it is the render surface of /expungement-ai/results, which the auditor itself proves is still in the route tree in its own claim about the second surface. ResultPanel.tsx:82-90 does present the referral outcome correctly ('consider legal aid or attorney review', tag 'Review needed'), so the correct presentation exists in the repo but sits on the orphaned surface while the live screening path shows the needs-more-info language. That makes the finding more damning, not less.

confirmed.requirement: No client-side code may infer eligibility, route, packet type or price.
confirmed.evidence: The result card's own header claims the opposite of what it does — ScreeningResult.tsx:4-5: "The frontend NEVER decides the outcome — it switches on the validated resultCode and renders what the engine returned." In fact, for the packet-path outcome the entire user-facing narrative is browser-authored and the engine's own output is discarded: :154 replaces evaluation.nextSteps with the hard-coded PACKET_READY_NEXT_STEPS (:94-99); :167 replaces evaluation.userLabel with a fixed title; :176-184 renders packetWhyText INSTEAD of evaluation.reasons, so the engine's source-backed reasons (each carrying a sourceRef) are dropped on exactly the outcome where the legal grounds matter most. packetWhyText itself asserts state law from the browser — :122 "This asks to remove the case from Alaska's public online court index. It does not erase all criminal-history records.", :123 "Nevada uses record sealing, not expungement.", :124 "A PATCH or PSP report may be needed before filing, but it is not needed before payment." Route character is inferred client-side by regex: :102 NON_CONVICTION_PATHWAY = /non-conviction|dismiss|no-disposition|acquit/i applied to evaluation.pathwayId at :104-106 and used at :112 and :119. Route identity is inferred client-side when the engine supplies no label: :155-158 falls back to routeLabelKeyForState, which at src/lib/expungement-ai/localization.ts:456-474 picks a route family from hard-coded state/substring rules (Alaska→CourtView Removal, Nevada→Record Sealing, Hawaii→Administrative Application, Delaware→Discretionary Expungement Packet, and substring matches on "marijuana"/"dismiss"/"summary"/"490"/"limited"/"seal"/"791"). That label is then rendered UNCONDITIONALLY at ScreeningResult.tsx:172-174 as the chip "{stateName}: {routeLabel}" — for every result code including hard_stop and not_covered_yet, where the engine selected no pathway at all. Price is a client-side literal, not an engine field: :248 "$50 one time when you are ready to generate this packet" (the server constant lives at src/lib/expungement-ai/consumer-payment-authority.ts:26 and never reaches the ScreeningEvaluation contract at frontend/contracts.ts:249-264). Finally src/lib/expungement-ai/missing-fields.ts:94-131 rewrites engine reason and next-step text in the browser (see the attorney-review finding).
confirmed.gapDetail: Packet type is the one item genuinely kept away from the browser (packetType is absent from the frontend ScreeningEvaluation contract and is derived server-side at authoritative-screening-result.ts:80-95). Eligibility narrative, route naming and price are all inferred or authored client-side.
confirmed.participantImpact: On a packet-path result the participant reads a hard-coded sentence about their own case rather than the engine's source-cited reasoning, and loses the statutory citations entirely. On an out-of-scope or hard-stop result they are still shown a route chip naming a specific remedy (e.g. "Nevada: Record Sealing") that the engine never selected for them.
confirmed.verifierNote: Every citation verified in current bytes. :154 substitutes the hard-coded PACKET_READY_NEXT_STEPS for evaluation.nextSteps; :167 substitutes a fixed title for evaluation.userLabel; :176-184 renders the single browser-authored packetWhyText INSTEAD of evaluation.reasons, so on the one outcome where legal grounds matter the engine's sourceRef-carrying reasons are dropped entirely (the .map over evaluation.reasons sits in the else-branch at :185-195). packetWhyText:122-124 does assert state law from the browser. NON_CONVICTION_PATHWAY regex at :102 is applied to pathwayId at :104-106. routeLabelKeyForState at localization.ts:456-474 is confirmed verbatim — hard-coded state rules for Alaska/Nevada/Hawaii/Delaware plus substring matching on marijuana/dismiss/summary/490/limited/seal/791 — and its output renders UNCONDITIONALLY as the '{stateName}: {routeLabel}' chip at :172-174, outside every conditional, so a hard_stop or not_covered_yet participant is shown a named remedy the engine never selected. Price: :248 is a literal; I confirmed frontend/contracts.ts:249-264 has no price field and CONSUMER_PACKET_PRICE_CENTS lives server-side at consumer-payment-authority.ts:26. The file header at :4-5 claiming 'The frontend NEVER decides the outcome' is contradicted by the file's own body. Nothing on any branch fixes the route-chip or packetWhyText behaviour.

confirmed.requirement: There must be exactly one preliminary-result surface, and it must go through the authoritative evaluator.
confirmed.evidence: A second surface exists and is still in the route tree: src/app/expungement-ai/results/page.tsx:20-24 computes an eligibility result on every GET from URL query parameters, via answersFromSearchParams (:39-60) which FABRICATES facts the participant never asserted — `sentence_completion_date: timing === "too_early" ? "No" : "Yes"` (:51), `disposition_date: "2020-01-01"` (:52), `state_exclusion_categories: ["None of these"]` (:53). It calls src/lib/expungement-ai/eligibility-adapter.ts:33-38 (evaluateExpungementAiMatter) directly, bypassing evaluateAuthoritativeScreeningResult and therefore the composed-route selection and the track-keyed deferral clamps. It then derives packet type from the result code alone (:117-121: any packet_ready → "custom_pleading"), contradicting the authoritative derivation from packetPlan.mode at authoritative-screening-result.ts:80-95, and hard-codes `priceCents: 5000` at :67. It renders ResultPanel, which at :155-168 presents an actual checkout Link to /expungement-ai/pay?briefcaseItemId=… with "Generate my packet - $50" (:23, :32, :159). Commit 56e64706 (merged; src/proxy.ts:125-128) removed /results from the expungement.ai host allowlist, asserting it is "an orphaned legacy route" that "throws InvalidAnswerError and 500s on every hit". That assertion is wrong: I checked the hard-coded answer id set against all 51 compiled profiles and 8 accept it in full — AK, AL, AR, IL, MO, NC, NY, TN. Only the page's default state=PA 500s. And src/proxy.ts:26-28 returns NextResponse.next() for any non-/internal path on a host that is not one of the four mapped public hosts, so /expungement-ai/results remains directly reachable on the application's own host.
confirmed.gapDetail: A browser-parameter-driven preliminary-result surface with a hard-coded pay gate is reachable for 8 jurisdictions, bypasses the authoritative evaluator, and infers packet type and price. The merged mitigation only covers one of the hosts, and its stated justification (500s on every hit) does not hold.
confirmed.participantImpact: Anyone who reaches /expungement-ai/results?state=IL&… is shown an eligibility outcome computed from a URL, built on dates and exclusion answers they never gave, together with a "Generate my packet - $50" checkout link.
confirmed.verifierNote: The requirement is genuinely unmet — a second surface exists, is reachable on the application's own host (proxy.ts:26-28 returns NextResponse.next() for any non-/internal path on an unmapped host), fabricates facts the participant never asserted (page.tsx:51-53: sentence_completion_date, disposition_date '2020-01-01', state_exclusion_categories ['None of these']), and calls runExpungementAiEligibilityCheck directly, bypassing evaluateAuthoritativeScreeningResult. But the auditor's severity assessment is WRONG and I measured it. I enumerated every URL-parameter combination the page can produce (4 caseOutcome x 5 recordCategory x timing x documents = 8,160 across all 51 compiled profiles) and ran the engine on each. Results: 2,560 evaluate, 5,600 throw InvalidAnswerError. SIXTEEN jurisdictions accept the hard-coded id set, not 8 — AK, AL, AR, AZ, CO, CT, DE, IL, MI, MO, NC, NJ, NY, TN, TX, VA. And ZERO of the 2,560 evaluating combinations returns packet_ready or packet_ready_with_caution with paymentAllowed=true; every single one returns needs_more_info with paymentAllowed=false. Since ResultPanel.tsx:112-114 gates on `paymentAllowed === true && packet-ready code`, the '$50 Generate my packet' checkout Link is UNREACHABLE from this surface, and eligibility-adapter.ts:67 leaves priceCents undefined and :117-121 leaves packetType undefined. Also, PA — the page's own default state — does throw, so the proxy comment at src/proxy.ts:125-128 is right about the default case even though 'every hit' overstates it. Corrected: a fabricated-answer preliminary result is reachable for 16 jurisdictions; the pay gate and the price/packet-type inference the auditor flagged are not.

confirmed.requirement: The result must be explicitly marked non-authoritative for payment on the wire, not merely by convention.
confirmed.evidence: The ScreeningEvaluation contract carries no such marker: src/lib/rcap-engine/contracts.ts:52-79 and src/lib/expungement-ai/frontend/contracts.ts:249-264 have no `preliminary`, `authoritativeForPayment` or equivalent field — the only payment-shaped field is `paymentAllowed: boolean` (contracts.ts:67), i.e. an affirmative signal on a preliminary result. The non-authoritative status is asserted only in prose comments (authoritative-screening-result.ts:19-22; pending/claim/route.ts:70-72; ScreeningResult.tsx:7-10). I searched all 617 remote branches for a wire marker (`git show <branch>:src/lib/rcap-engine/contracts.ts | grep -c "preliminary|nonAuthoritative|advisoryOnly"` across every branch) and found zero — this is not sitting unmerged anywhere. confirmed.requirement: The verification hash must be stable across a database round-trip
confirmed.evidence: In tree `packetVerificationHash` hashes the object as-is: `createHash("sha256").update(JSON.stringify(snapshot))` (src/lib/expungement-ai/packet-information.ts:865-867) — no canonicalization. `verifiedPacketRecordFromDraft` builds that snapshot by spreading draft entries then appending `schemaVersion`/`verifiedAt` without canonicalizing (packet-information.ts:766-783), and the hash is recomputed and compared after the snapshot has round-tripped through Postgres jsonb in `protectedAuthoritySnapshotFor` (packet-information.ts:605-608). jsonb does not preserve key order, so the recomputed hash can differ from the stored one, making `protectedAuthoritySnapshotFor` return null → `protectedPacketInformationModelFor` null → `{status:"invalidated", reason:"protected_verification_dependencies_changed"}` (packet-information.ts:440-442). Note `protectedPacketDraftHash` (packet-information.ts:755-757) already canonicalizes, so drafts are unaffected — only the final verified snapshot. The fix is on the unmerged branch: bef2f5ff changes it to `JSON.stringify(canonicalize(snapshot))` and exports it.
confirmed.gapDetail: This is over-invalidation rather than under-invalidation, so it fails safe — but it makes verification non-durable, which is indistinguishable to the participant from the system losing their attestation.
confirmed.participantImpact: A participant who verifies, closes the tab, and returns can find their verification silently reverted to unverified with no explanation.
confirmed.verifierNote: Confirmed line by line, including the mechanism. verifiedPacketRecordFromDraft (packet-information.ts:766-783) strips capturedAt/schemaVersion from the canonically-ordered draft, spreads the remainder, then APPENDS schemaVersion and verifiedAt last — so the object's key order is not canonical (a canonical sort would place schemaVersion between resultCode and screeningAnswers). packetVerificationHash then hashes JSON.stringify of that insertion order with no canonicalize call, while protectedPacketDraftHash 110 lines earlier DOES canonicalize — the asymmetry is visible in the same file. The recompute-and-compare happens post-round-trip at protectedAuthoritySnapshotFor:606-607, and Postgres jsonb does not preserve key order, so the comparison can fail and cascade to {status:'invalidated', reason:'protected_verification_dependencies_changed'} (:440-442). I confirmed the fix diff on the branch: `-function packetVerificationHash(...JSON.stringify(snapshot))` → `+export function packetVerificationHash(...JSON.stringify(canonicalize(snapshot)))`. Fails safe (over-invalidation) but makes verification non-durable.

confirmed.requirement: Credit rule: failed packet generation = 0 credits
confirmed.evidence: Happy path is correct: src/lib/expungement-ai/packet-generation.ts:120-163 builds the artifact in memory and only returns protectedSponsorship on success; a throw lands in the catch at :150-163 which sets packetStatus='failed' and never calls any credit RPC. But supabase/migrations/20260818202000_rcap_upgrade_02_functions.sql:5886-5895 (the cap_reached_no_overage branch of record_partner_packet_generation) sets `claimed_slot_state = 'consumed'` (:5888) and then returns recorded=false / counted_as='not_counted', while recompute_rcap_partner_entitlements rebuilds screenings_used as `count(sessions where claimed_slot_state='consumed')` (:6386, :6393).
confirmed.gapDetail: A generation that was REFUSED for cap exhaustion — the participant got nothing — leaves the session marked 'consumed'. The next `npm run expungement:recompute-rcap-entitlements` (package.json:191) therefore charges the partner one credit for a packet that was never produced. The refusal and the ledger disagree.
confirmed.participantImpact: A partner is billed for packets their participants never received, and the inflated screenings_used pushes other participants over the cap sooner.
confirmed.verifierNote: CONFIRMED. I read supabase/migrations/20260818202000_rcap_upgrade_02_functions.sql:5818-5926 in full. So the next recompute converts that refusal into a billed credit. The in-memory happy path IS correct (packet-generation.ts:123-163 catch sets 'failed' and calls no credit RPC), so PARTIAL is the right grade. `git log --all -S"claimed_slot_state = 'consumed'" -- supabase/migrations/` returns only the two schema-baseline commits — no branch fixes it.

confirmed.requirement: Credit rule: the first successful sponsored packet consumes exactly 1 credit, atomically, at the moment of Ready
confirmed.evidence: The exactly-once semantics live entirely in the unmerged RPC: it takes the item FOR UPDATE (bef2f5ff:...:984), refuses on verification/source mismatch (:985-993), short-circuits to already_finalized when packet_artifact_json is already set (:997-1006), calls record_partner_packet_generation exactly once (:1008), and only then writes the artifact and packet_status='ready' in the same transaction (:1012-1022). The underlying single-credit increment is in tree at supabase/migrations/20260818202000_rcap_upgrade_02_functions.sql:5845-5867, gated on claimed_slot_state='claimed' (:5843-5848) so a second call returns 'already_recorded'. What is missing in tree is the wrapper that makes credit-consumption and Ready one transaction.
confirmed.gapDetail: In tree there is no path that consumes a sponsored credit at all: the wrapper RPC does not exist, and nothing else calls record_partner_packet_generation (the only other wrapper, recordPartnerPacketGeneration at rcap-slot-lifecycle.ts:129-172, has zero callers).
confirmed.participantImpact: Zero sponsored packets and zero sponsored credits on mainline. Partners see no usage; participants see a 409.

FOR UPDATE on consumer_briefcase_items, refuses on verification/source mismatch, short-circuits to 'already_finalized' when packet_artifact_json is already set (with a three-way equality check on hash/entitlement_source/artifact), calls record_partner_packet_generation once, then sets packet_status='ready' in the same transaction. The single-credit increment IS in tree at 20260818202000:5843-5867 gated on claimed_slot_state='claimed'. What is missing is the wrapper. confirmed.requirement: Overage packets must be accounted separately from included credits
confirmed.evidence: supabase/migrations/20260818202000_rcap_upgrade_02_functions.sql:5876-5885 increments overage_packets and overage_amount_cents WITHOUT incrementing screenings_used, then falls through to :5899-5901 which sets claimed_slot_state='consumed'. recompute_rcap_partner_entitlements (:6386, :6393) then rebuilds screenings_used as the count of ALL consumed sessions, including overage ones.

confirmed.verifierNote: CONFIRMED. 20260818202000:5876-5885 increments overage_packets and overage_amount_cents and sets v_counted:='overage' WITHOUT touching screenings_used, then falls through to the shared tail at :5899-5901 which sets claimed_slot_state='consumed'. recompute at :6386-6393 then counts that same session into screenings_used. confirmed.requirement: Sponsorship record controls WHO is covered

confirmed.requirement: Sponsorship record controls WHICH program / event
confirmed.evidence: The session records partner_access_code_id, campaign_name and attribution_source (supabase/migrations/20260818202000_rcap_upgrade_02_functions.sql:211-219) and per-code analytics are aggregated at :884-905 (get_partner_code_analytics) and surfaced by src/lib/partners/partner-access-codes.ts:424-443. The legacy supabase/phase-35c-rcap-claim-screening-session.sql:51-65 DID enforce it with a conditional `update ... where pe.screenings_used < pe.screenings_allowed` returning 'capacity_full' on not-found — dropped by the applied migration. confirmed.requirement: Sponsorship record controls GEOGRAPHY (test: wrong geography)

confirmed.requirement: Sponsorship must be re-confirmed as CURRENTLY VALID at the moment of packet generation, not merely at screening claim
confirmed.evidence: At claim time the partner must be paid/qualified/provisioned (supabase/migrations/20260818202000_rcap_upgrade_02_functions.sql:126-134) and the code must be active and unexpired (:148-152). confirmed.gapDetail: The contract requires the server to 'confirm valid partner/event sponsorship' at packet-ready. What is actually confirmed is a boolean stamped onto the session at screening start, possibly weeks earlier.
confirmed.participantImpact: A partner whose contract lapsed, whose provisioning was revoked, or whose campaign code was disabled keeps having credits consumed by every session claimed before the change.
confirmed.verifierNote: CONFIRMED. Claim time genuinely checks partner_records.payment_status IN ('paid','demo_paid') AND qualification_status='qualified' AND provisioning_status IN ('provisioned','active') (20260818202000:126-134) plus code validity (:148-152). None of that is re-read at generation. I traced the full generation path: packet-generation.ts:109 -> requireCurrentPacketSponsorshipAuthority:445-461 reads only product/partnerBenefitActive/partnerSlug/sourceSessionId from the trusted source; rcap-slot-lifecycle.ts resolvePartnerPacketCapDecision reads only screening_sessions + partner_entitlement; record_partner_packet_generation:5828-5842 checks only flow_mode/partner_slug/partner_benefit_active. I read the unmerged finalizer myself — bef2f5ff:988-992 checks the same three session fields and nothing on partner_records or partner_access_codes. So even the unmerged branch does not close this. confirmed.requirement: Sponsorship must not bypass packet-family authority and form-set authority
confirmed.evidence: The consumer lane enforces this at src/lib/expungement-ai/payment-adapter.ts:594-608 assertCheckoutAllowed — assertNotExactDeferral (:536-543), assertNotComponentDeferral (:545-551), assertNotTerminalTreatment (:557-563), assertPacketRouteCanDeliver (:580-591, refusing any route whose rendererKind is 'none'), and a packet-family membership test (`packetType === custom_pleading | official_pdf_overlay | legacy_packet`, :601-608). It is called from exactly one place: payment-adapter.ts:171 (createConsumerPacketCheckout). The durable render lane has its own equivalent at src/lib/rcap/render/job-contract.ts:319. The sponsored lane's only gate is src/lib/expungement-ai/packet-generation.ts:348-371, which checks resultCode membership and (when paymentRequired) payment authority — and sponsored callers pass paymentRequired=false (packet-generation.ts:111, :180, :434).

confirmed.requirement: Sponsorship must not bypass packet-credit rules (the per-route creditConsumable authority)

In src/ it appears ONLY in packet-route-resolver.ts — the type declaration at :38 and eleven literal assignments (:99,:123,:162,:185,:210,:230,:247,:263,:279,:293,:312), true only at :247 for legacy_verified. Outside the resolver it is read only by three offline scripts (rcap-hosted-checkout-gate.mjs, generate-rcap-problematic-pdf-master-list.mjs, generate-rcap-track-terminalization.mjs). confirmed.requirement: Sponsorship must not bypass render-job authority (sponsored packets should flow through the durable, fenced, checksum-validated render pipeline)
confirmed.evidence: src/lib/rcap/render/job-queue.ts:75-105 defines a sponsored RenderJobIdentity and :124-155 enqueueRenderJob passes p_partner_id when mode==='sponsored'. confirmed.verifierNote: CONFIRMED, including the cascade. job-queue.ts:79-84 defines the sponsored RenderJobIdentity and :141 passes `p_partner_id: sponsored ? identity.partnerId : null`. grep for enqueueRenderJob across src/ and scripts/ returns the definition at job-queue.ts:124 plus three verifier/test references and nothing else — no runtime caller. confirmed.requirement: One coherent packet-credit ledger for sponsored packets

confirmed.gapDetail: For /partner/clinic/* and /api/clinic/*, the ten clinic RLS policies at supabase/migrations/20260825121000_clinic_mode_security.sql:459-477 are never evaluated at runtime. confirmed.verifierNote: Confirmed byte-for-byte. src/lib/supabase/server.ts:6,17 builds getSupabaseAdminClient() from process.env.SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY. src/lib/clinic-mode/service.ts requireDatabase() returns exactly that client and backs listClinicEvents (query .eq('partner_slug', actor.partnerSlug) hand-written), getClinicEventWorkspace (event + clinic_event_staff + clinic_event_access_codes + clinic_event_audit limit 100, none scoped by anything but the hand filter), and assertEventScope. By contrast src/lib/partners/partner-dashboard-rls-repository.ts:111 does use createServerSupabaseAuthClient() with no partner_slug filter, so the mainline dashboard genuinely honors the spec and the Clinic surfaces genuinely do not — the divergence the auditor describes is real. confirmed.requirement: Every partner tenant must have at least one active partner_admin
confirmed.evidence: The only enforcement is a launch blocker, and it does not check the role. src/lib/partners/partner-onboarding.ts:257 computes the count as `.from('partner_users').select('id',{count:'exact',head:true}).eq('partner_slug',slug).eq('status','active').in('role',['partner_admin','partner_staff'])` — i.e. `adminUserCount` counts staff. :759 then reads `if (view.adminUserCount < 1 && !view.sections.adminUsersReady) blockers.push('Invite at least one partner admin.')`, so the check is additionally short-circuited by a stored boolean. That boolean is set unconditionally by src/lib/partners/partner-onboarding.ts:630 `patchOnboarding(supabase, slug, { admin_users_ready: true })` inside `recordAdminInvited`, whose only caller is src/app/api/internal/partners/onboarding/[partnerSlug]/route.ts:131 — invoked at :122-126 with `role: payload.role ?? 'partner_admin'`, so inviting a partner_staff flips the flag too. Provisioning deliberately creates no membership at all (supabase/migrations/20260819120000_rcap_partner_provisioning.sql:16-17 'no Auth user, no membership, no invitation'), and the membership row is inserted with `status:'active'` before the invite is ever accepted (src/lib/partners/add-partner-user.ts:329).
confirmed.gapDetail: No invariant — DB constraint, trigger, or runtime check — guarantees a live tenant has ≥1 active partner_admin. A tenant whose only admin is removed, or that was launched after inviting a single partner_staff, passes the gate. There is also no runtime path to set `partner_users.status='disabled'` (grep across src/ finds no UPDATE/DELETE against partner_users at all), so a departed admin's access can only be revoked by direct database access.
confirmed.participantImpact: A clinic can go live with no one authorized to pause the event, revoke a compromised access code, or manage staff — and a departed staff member's access cannot be revoked through the product.
confirmed.verifierNote: Confirmed line-for-line. partner-onboarding.ts:257 counts partner_users with .in('role', ['partner_admin','partner_staff']) — so adminUserCount is not an admin count. :759 reads `if (view.adminUserCount < 1 && !view.sections.adminUsersReady)`, so the stored boolean alone satisfies the blocker; :630 recordAdminInvited() sets admin_users_ready: true unconditionally, and its caller src/app/internal/partners/onboarding/[partnerSlug]/route.ts invokes it with `role: payload.role ?? 'partner_admin'` — inviting a partner_staff flips it. confirmed.requirement: The follow-up queue must not expose more case detail than the role permits
confirmed.evidence: The strong parts are real: `clinic_get_event_queue` (supabase/migrations/20260825122000_clinic_mode_accounting_reporting.sql:373-402) returns no name, email, phone, matter_id or screening_session_id, and for non-privileged staff restricts rows to cases whose assisted session is still active and unexpired (:394-399); `clinic_transition_event_case` re-checks the same at :419-422. The participant's Briefcase stays owner-only (supabase/migrations/20260728213131_remote_schema.sql:2594 `consumer briefcase select own items` USING `auth.uid() = user_id`), and src/components/clinic-mode/ClinicQueueClient.tsx:18 renders only the last 8 characters of the participant UUID. Two gaps: (1) the RPC returns identical columns to every role — participant_user_id, county_name, court_name, jurisdiction, court_identity_verified — with no role-differentiated redaction, only row filtering, and the JSON body of src/app/api/clinic/events/[eventId]/queue/route.ts:13 carries the full UUID the UI truncates; (2) because `clinic_cases` is directly SELECT-able by any staff holding 'queue' under `clinic_cases_scoped_read` (supabase/migrations/20260825121000_clinic_mode_security.sql:469, granted to authenticated at :488-491), a staff member querying the table through PostgREST rather than the RPC also gets `matter_id`, `assisted_session_id` and `screening_session_id`, and gets them for expired sessions — strictly more than the curated RPC exposes. Likewise `clinic_get_follow_ups` (:426-444) returns `internal_notes` to every holder of 'follow_up' with no redaction tier.
confirmed.gapDetail: Column-level least-privilege is enforced only in the RPC projection, not by the policy surface the same role can reach directly; and the RPC's active-session row filter is absent from the table policy.
confirmed.participantImpact: Approved event staff can read the identifiers linking a participant to their saved matter and screening session for cases whose assistance window has already expired.
confirmed.verifierNote: Confirmed, and the auditor is fair to both sides. The strong parts are real: clinic_get_event_queue's projection omits name/email/phone/matter_id/screening_session_id and adds an active-unexpired-assisted-session row filter for non-privileged staff; the participant Briefcase stays owner-only under `consumer briefcase select own items` USING auth.uid()=user_id; ClinicQueueClient truncates the participant UUID to 8 chars. The two gaps are also real. (1) The RPC returns an identical column set to every role — row filtering, not column redaction — and the API JSON at src/app/api/clinic/events/[eventId]/queue/route.ts carries the full participant UUID that the UI merely truncates client-side. (2) clinic_cases_scoped_read is a table policy granted to authenticated, so a staff member holding 'queue' reaching clinic_cases through PostgREST directly gets matter_id, assisted_session_id and screening_session_id, and gets them without the RPC's active-session filter — strictly more than the curated RPC. clinic_get_follow_ups returns internal_notes to every 'follow_up' holder with no tier. I confirmed no column-level GRANT/REVOKE narrows any clinic table: the only `grant select (` in the migrations (20260818209000:171-197) is column-level anon access to the six CONTENT tables, nothing under clinic_ or rcap_. This is a defense-in-depth gap rather than a cross-tenant break, which matches the medium confidence and PARTIAL status. Claim stands.

confirmed.requirement: Partner-tenant reporting must not surface per-participant case detail to partner roles
confirmed.evidence: The rendered dashboards are aggregate-only — src/lib/partners/partner-dashboard-rls-repository.ts:227-247 (`summarizeIntake`/`summarizeDocuments`) reduce fetched rows to counts and a latest date. But the underlying RLS grant is row-level, not aggregate-level: supabase/migrations/20260728213131_remote_schema.sql:2808 `rcap_intake_sessions_select_own_partner` grants SELECT on the whole row to any active partner_admin OR partner_staff of the tenant, and `GRANT ALL ON TABLE public.rcap_intake_sessions TO authenticated` (:3306) means the same session token works directly against PostgREST. That table carries `user_first_name`, `user_last_name`, `user_email`, `user_phone`, `state`, `county`, `record_type`, `charge_or_case_type`, `case_outcome`, `approximate_case_year` (:1823-1832). The same shape applies to rcap_document_packets (:2796) and rcap_briefcase_items (:2784). Separately, src/lib/partner-dashboard-data.ts:272-277 seeds a `recentActivity` table of per-user rows (`{ userId: 'User-1084', state: 'District of Columbia', status: 'Filed', outcome: 'Pending' }`) which feeds the report builders (src/lib/reports/partner-weekly-report-data.ts:7,:226) — currently only as a count (src/lib/reports/render-weekly-report-html.ts:129), and the module's own note at :286-287 says 'Replace this seeded layer with live loaders'.
confirmed.gapDetail: Nothing at the data layer restricts a partner role to aggregates. The privacy property holds only because the two rendered surfaces happen to aggregate; a partner_staff bypassing the UI reads full participant PII rows for their tenant. There is no aggregate-only view, no column-level grant, and no separation between the reporting role and the operational role.
confirmed.participantImpact: Any partner staff account can pull every participant's name, email, phone, charge type and case outcome for that partner — far beyond what a 'view approved aggregate reports' permission implies.
confirmed.verifierNote: Confirmed. rcap_intake_sessions_select_own_partner is FOR SELECT TO authenticated USING (partner_slug = current_partner_slug()) — a whole-row grant. current_partner_slug() (:400-409) resolves for any active partner_users row with role in ('partner_admin','partner_staff'), so staff and admin are indistinguishable at the policy layer. GRANT ALL ON TABLE rcap_intake_sessions TO authenticated at :3306 means the same browser session token reaches PostgREST directly. The table columns confirmed at :1819-1832 include user_first_name, user_last_name, user_email, user_phone, state, county, record_type, charge_or_case_type, case_outcome, approximate_case_year. I searched every later migration (2026081*, 20260819*, 2026082*) for any GRANT/REVOKE touching rcap_intake_sessions / rcap_document_packets / rcap_briefcase_items: zero hits — nothing narrows it afterward, and the only column-level grant in the repo is the anon/content-table one at 20260818209000:171. The privacy property therefore holds only at the presentation layer: I read src/lib/partners/partner-dashboard-rls-repository.ts summarizeIntake/summarizeDocuments and they do reduce to counts plus a latest date, exactly as the auditor said — which is precisely why the property is presentational, not enforced. No aggregate-only view or reporting-scoped grant exists. Claim stands.

confirmed.requirement: Access-code administrative actions must be attributable in the audit trail
confirmed.evidence: src/lib/partners/partner-access-codes.ts:445-465 `appendAccessCodeEvent` inserts into `rcap_record_events` with a literal `actor: 'partner_admin'` (:459) regardless of who actually acted, and records no auth_user_id. confirmed.verifierNote: Confirmed, and this is the strongest of the ten. confirmed.evidence: Three real adversarial suites exist. (1) scripts/clinic-mode/verify-schema-rls.mjs applies the three clinic migrations into PGlite, seeds tenant-a/tenant-b (:259-268), and asserts denial as the actual `authenticated` role with `set_config('request.jwt.claim.sub', ...)` (:328-341) — :145, :146, :231, :237. I executed it: passes. (2) scripts/verify-onboarding-tenant-isolation.mjs:1-5 states its purpose exactly ('the only proof is connecting as one tenant's user and failing to reach another tenant's rows') and covers cross-tenant read/update/insert/delete (:152,:164,:177,:194) plus a null-auth.uid() case (:143); it aborts without RCAP_TEST_DATABASE_URL. (3) scripts/verify-partner-dashboard-rls-isolation.mjs drives real browser sessions for four identities and covers ?partnerSlug= override (:277-278) and unauthenticated denial (:367,:381); it requires eight live credentials. Wiring is the gap: `grep -c clinic package.json` = 0, so none of scripts/clinic-mode/* is reachable from any npm script or CI workflow; the dashboard suite is only the standalone `partners:verify-dashboard-rls-isolation` (package.json:43) and the onboarding suite only `partners:verify-onboarding-tenant-isolation` (package.json:292) — neither is in the `test` script (package.json:12) or in any .github/workflows file.

confirmed.participantImpact: A regression that re-opens cross-tenant participant access would not be caught by the default test run.
